data.cultural_impact: The name Amitava is deeply rooted in Hindu culture. In Hindu mythology, the name Amitava is associated with Lord Shiva, referring to his infinite love and compassion towards his devotees. It is also the name of several other deities, including Amitava, the goddess of happiness and prosperity, and Amitaba, the god of infinite love and mercy. Additionally, the name Amitava is the title of many esteemed scholars, sages, and philosophers in Hindu tradition, symbolizing their vast knowledge and wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Amitava lies in its symbolism of infinite love, compassion, and wisdom. The name invokes a sense of infinite love and compassion, inspiring one to cultivate a similar attitude towards all beings. Furthermore, the name Amitava is a reminder of the infinite wisdom that resides within each individual, inspiring one to seek knowledge and understanding in all aspects of life. historical_references.reference: Amitavakadi Maharaja (1352-1375 AD) was a powerful king of the Sena dynasty in Bengal. He ruled over a vast territory that included present-day West Bengal and parts of Bihar and Orissa. His name 'Amitav' means 'The Incomparable God'. He defeated the Mongols in several battles and maintained peace and prosperity in his kingdom.

Amitava Shastri (1901-1972) was a renowned Indian scholar and philosopher. He was born in a Brahmin family in Barendra, Bengal Presidency, British India. He contributed significantly to the field of Indian philosophy, particularly Advaita Vedanta. His works include 'The Concept of the Self in the Bhagavadgita' and 'Jivanmukti Viveka'.
